CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female here for her annual visit. She reports she has been doing better overall but has been struggling with depression on and off over the past year, particularly due to being trapped inside and working remotely. She is currently on Prozac 20 mg daily, which she reports has helped her in the past. She feels that increasing the dose may help her through this difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that she has been managing. The pain is worse with prolonged sitting at her desk at work and improves with movement and position changes. She experiences some numbness in the extremities described as feeling like they are "falling asleep," but denies tingling or leg pain. Symptoms improve with standing and position changes. She denies weakness in her legs. She is able to perform activities of daily living, exercise, and go to the store, though symptoms are bothersome with extremes of prolonged sitting or standing. She has a history of congenital coronary artery disease requiring coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies tingling or pain down legs. Denies weakness in legs. Able to perform activities of daily living.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congenital coronary artery disease with coronary artery bypass grafting in childhood
Depression
Chronic back pain

MEDICATIONS
Prozac 20 mg daily
Aspirin

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at a desk. Recently working remotely.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Does not appear in distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiac: Three out of six systolic ejection murmur, stable
Lungs: Clear
Abdomen: Soft
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine, decreased flexion of back, good lower extremity strength, no edema

RESULTS
ECG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg daily (one tablet once a day). Patient to continue on current regimen.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy for symptom management. Patient declines pain medication at this time. Physical therapy referral ordered.
3. Coronary artery disease history: Order echocardiogram. Continue Aspirin 81 mg daily.
Nurse to assist with scheduling tests and follow-up.
